interest: Shows Ceylon's Catholic outrage over Japan's 1948 abortion bill, and Japan's postwar overhaul of child welfare toward family-centered care.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file (decimal file 894.4055) from the U.S. State Department's central decimal files covers matters of maternal and child welfare, social legislation, and moral customs in occupied Japan during 1948. The file contains two distinct groups of records: diplomatic correspondence from the American Consulate General in Colombo, Ceylon, transmitting a Catholic editorial strongly protesting Japan's proposed legalization of abortion and urging the United States as the occupying power to intervene; and despatches from the Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan in Tokyo forwarding official English translations of key Japanese child welfare legislation. These Japanese records include Cabinet Order No. 11 and Ministry of Welfare Enforcement Regulations for the landmark Child Welfare Law of 1947, as well as Children's Bureau Directive Ji-Hatsu No. 50 ('Functioning of Family Care'), which set forth extensive regulations, standards, and administrative forms for foster home placement, institutional supervision, child labor safeguards, and domestic adoption.

subfiles.about: Ministerial ordinance setting detailed operational rules for Child Welfare Centers, health guidance, maternal handbooks, foster placement, and nursery teacher testing.
subfiles.summary: Promulgated as Kosei Shorei No. 11, this ministerial ordinance establishes comprehensive administrative regulations under the Child Welfare Law. It defines the establishment, jurisdiction, and supervisory functions of Child Welfare Centers; health guidance procedures; and rules for issuing, using, and returning Maternal-and-Child Handbooks (including access to special rations). The regulations also establish procedures for institutional admission, foster home registries, examination standards and subjects for nursery teachers, expense reimbursements, and the repeal of prewar child welfare and anti-cruelty ordinances.
subfiles.title: Enforcement Regulation of Child Welfare Law (Ministry of Welfare Ordinance No. 11)

subfiles.about: Cabinet order governing the composition of child welfare boards, personnel qualifications, juvenile institutions, and public subsidy allocations.
subfiles.summary: Cabinet Order sets up Japan's Child Welfare Boards and officials, mandates reform facilities, and funds aid for indigent mothers.
subfiles.title: Cabinet Order for Enforcement of Child Welfare Law

subfiles.about: Administrative directive and standardized forms establishing comprehensive procedures for foster care, child labor regulation, and legal adoption.
subfiles.from: Children's Bureau, Ministry of Welfare, Japan
subfiles.summary: Issued as directive Ji-Hatsu No. 50, this document sets forth detailed instructions and philosophy for promoting family foster care and legal adoption over institutionalization for dependent, neglected, and orphaned children. It prescribes strict criteria for investigating prospective foster homes, supervising child nutrition, schooling, and health, and regulating work under the Labor Standards Law, strictly forbidding child exploitation and hazardous labor. The directive also details adoption procedures coordinated through Child Welfare Centers and the Court of Domestic Relations (Family Court), and provides five official application and investigation forms (Forms No. 1 through No. V).
subfiles.title: Children's Bureau Directive Ji-Hatsu No. 50: 'Functioning of Family Care'
subfiles.to: Prefectural Governors and Child Welfare Centers
